notes: One or more validated on-foot poses per body, each taken from a live capture of the player standing on that body. Each is a reachable standing position, not an authored landing site and not a claim about the rest of the body. Where a body carries two poses they stand in different places, and often in different workspaces; the ids say which.
Bodies absent from this document have no capture of the player standing on them. Absence is an unresolved gap, not evidence that the body is unlandable.
Positions are raw signed engine longwords in the body-local surface grid at 65,536 units per cell. The yaw word wraps every 1024 units with north at $0200 modulo $0400, rising clockwise.
The yaw word is published raw and carries bits above $03FF; only its low ten bits are the bearing, as the existing Eris presentation document already assumes.

bodyTurn is the Body's rotation accumulator at $0062EA + 4 x body, one turn every $04000000, and subStellarLongitude is $79BE, the Body's sub-stellar longitude in the same 1024-step angle as the yaw. Together with the position they decide the terminator at $050562; each pose's answer agrees with the engine day flag $7A4E. The sub-stellar longitude is a table atan2 of the Body's centre and is read, not recomputed; on DAMOCLES, whose centre moves, it is the value its arrival wrote.

The cell is read from the engine cell word $7B5C, the same word the resident object and object-drop matchers compare against. Where the body has a recovered 16x16 workspace origin, the camera longwords reproduce that cell independently and workspaceOrigin carries the origin.

A 16x16 workspace is a window onto a body surface that spans thousands of cells, so one body can carry several. Where the longwords put a pose outside the one recovered workspace on its body, workspaceOrigin is null and the evidence field says so; impliedWorkspaceOrigin always carries the origin that pose's own longwords and cell imply, so an unanchored cell can be anchored later without guessing. Two poses that agree on an implied origin stand in the same window.
Source memstates are Restricted Material and are not published; their SHA-256 values identify them.

Almost every memstate behind this document was captured by an IPF-capable Hatari 2.6.1 build and rehosted onto the pinned build by research/damocles-st/scripts/memstate-rehost.py (#331); eris-spaceport-onfoot was captured on the pinned build already and its container is passed through byte for byte. Only the snapshot container changes: each pose decodes to the same words and the same ramSha256 as before, and all of them restore and run in the pinned laboratory.

memstateSha256 identifies the rehosted container and ramSha256 the machine inside it. ramSha256 is the stable identity: it is unchanged for every pose this document has ever carried. memstateSha256 moved once, when rehosting was made byte-reproducible - gzip had been stamping the wall clock into the container header, so one captured memstate produced a different hash on every rehost. The containers the earlier hashes named hold the same bytes apart from that timestamp.
